contributions: A reframing of steerability measurement from how far a model moves toward a target to what kind of response it gives when it declines, with rubrics derived from observed behaviour because the space of response modes could not be specified in advance.

A peer-judging design in which all six models judge all responses blind against fixed rubrics, with ground truth as a leave-one-out consensus excluding self-judgment -- which is what makes a self-preference check possible, and it finds no judge leaning either way.

The finding that frontier models differ categorically rather than in degree, with one model withholding reasoning while answering on 99 of 100 steered items against 0 in 500 for the rest, and an almost eightfold spread on values-consistent refusal.

An audit suite carrying equal weight to the results: a token-budget confound found and removed, a hypothesis-blind judge-prompt control, and a full rerun on the 80 percent of items written after the rubrics were frozen, which preserves every ordering and improves inter-judge agreement.

A prompt-only probing control that is the right shape and rarely run -- training the identical probe on a small model that never produced the responses, establishing that 0.72 balanced accuracy is available from prompt ambiguity alone, so only the margin above it is attributable to the model's own state.

A steering sweep sized against the residual norm at the injection layer, with the direction defined on half the items and evaluated on the other half, showing monotone behavioural change across the full range and reporting the truncation cost that accompanies suppression.
datasets: author-constructed paired steering benchmark (300 items, three categories, plus 40 validation items)
limitations: Stated repeatedly and specifically. The suppression-resistance finding rests on the category with the lowest inter-judge agreement (0.599 against 0.767-0.854 elsewhere) and the same category is where removing the item-context field changed the most labels, which the authors attribute to that rubric asking for the study's finest distinctions. Nine comparisons significant on the full sample fall below threshold on the held-out subset, all in that same category. The mechanistic section carries an explicit boundary: the logged responses were generated by a hosted serving stack while activations were harvested from reference weights run locally, so the computation is not byte-identical, and the authors state the section is illustrative for those reference weights rather than a causal explanation of the cross-model differences observed in deployment. One reasoning-elicitation observation from a keyword scan rather than the consensus rubric is reported as a quantified preliminary observation rather than a result. Not stated but worth noticing: the probe rests on 100 items and 20 layers, the steering direction on 50, and the behavioural findings are about six specific model versions at one point in time, several of which will have been replaced; the strongest claims are of the form 'this mode appears in only one of six models', which is a statement about the evaluated sample rather than about model families.
method: Three hundred paired items across values-conflict, reasoning-elicitation and reasoning-suppression, plus 40 validation items, each a base prompt with its steered version, with all six models seeing identical items in both conditions so item difficulty cannot masquerade as a model difference. Because the space of response behaviours could not be specified in advance, rubrics were derived from observed behaviour in a development phase; all six models then applied those rubrics at scale as blind peer judges, producing 24,480 judgments scored by leave-one-out consensus that excludes each model's judgments of itself. The auditing is where most of the work is. A token-budget confound was found and removed. A control experiment re-judged a balanced sample of 216 responses twice, once with the judge prompt repeated exactly and once with the item-context field removed, to measure whether the prompt leaked the study's expectations. The entire analysis was rerun on only the 80 items per category written after the rubrics were frozen. A self-preference check compared each judge's disagreement with consensus on its own outputs against other models'. Two validation categories test whether the instrument works at all: stylistic items with a verifiable formatting instruction, and reasoning-hint items whose correct answers can be checked externally. The mechanistic half then targets the largest within-model baseline split -- one open-weight model divides its unsteered values-conflict responses 42 clarification-seeking derails to 58 substantive answers -- by rebuilding each exact prompt, feeding the exact logged response back through the reference weights, and recording the residual stream at the last token of the response, where the model has committed. Probes are L2 logistic regressions over 8,192 dimensions with only 100 examples, so three guards are applied: stratified five-fold cross-validation, a nested inner loop choosing the penalty so no probe choice sees its scoring data, and a permutation test shuffling labels and rerunning the whole pipeline 200 times per layer. Balanced accuracy is reported. Steering uses the difference of class means, unit-normalised, taken at a layer in the middle of the accuracy plateau so half the network remains ahead of the intervention, with the 100 items split once into 50 that define the direction and 50 held out, and strengths sized against the median residual norm at that layer so the sweep spans a quarter to roughly all of the stream's own magnitude, under greedy decoding.
one_liner: Measures not how far six frontier models move under steering pressure but what kind of response they give when they decline, finds several response modes belonging to a single model, and then traces the largest within-model split to a linearly decodable and causally steerable direction in an open-weight model's residual stream.
problem: Developers describe distinct approaches to values training, but whether those differences produce measurably different behaviour under pressure has not been directly studied. Existing steerability evaluations all ask the same question -- did the output hit the requested target -- whether the target is a verifiable formatting constraint, a community norm, or a vector in attribute space. None asks what the model does when it declines, which is where the safety-relevant variation lives, and none can distinguish a model that refuses a compromised framing while offering an alternative from one that simply fails to comply.

relevance.reasoning-interpretability: The mechanistic section is short but it is the best-controlled probe-and-steer result in the archive, and two of its controls should become standard here. The first is the prompt-only baseline: the identical probe is trained on a small model that never produced any of the responses, and it reaches 0.72 balanced accuracy -- because the items being classified are, by construction, more ambiguous as prompts, and any competent model represents prompt ambiguity. So the 70B model's 0.87 plateau is only worth about 14 points above what the prompt alone supplies. Almost no probing result in this archive reports that decomposition, and without it a high held-out accuracy cannot distinguish 'the model has decided' from 'the input was ambiguous'. The second is the intervention's scale reference: strengths are sized against the median residual norm at the injection layer rather than chosen in raw units, which is exactly the correction the archive's measurement-audit material shows is necessary before any steering number means anything across settings. The layer choice is also justified rather than picked -- mid-plateau, so half the network's depth remains ahead of the intervention to act on -- and the direction is defined on 50 items and evaluated on the other 50, so it is not scored on what built it. What the result then shows is a genuinely monotone dose-response across the full sweep, from 0 percent derail at the strongest negative push through a 40 percent zero-control to 86 percent at the strongest positive, with the zero-control landing within two points of the rate seen in the original hosted evaluation. That last check quietly validates the whole setup, since the responses were generated on a serving stack and the activations harvested from reference weights. The cost is reported in the same table and is the part to carry: at the strongest suppression 28 of 50 generations truncate, against 0 of 50 at the strongest push the other way. So the direction is not symmetric in its side effects, and a paper reporting only the derail rate would have shown a clean bidirectional result while half its suppressed outputs were broken. Read alongside the archive's bidirectional-steering material, this is a case where the effect reverses but the damage does not. On the behavioural side, the design is worth borrowing wherever the archive uses model judges: rubrics derived from observed behaviour rather than specified in advance, all judges blind, consensus computed leave-one-out so self-judgment is excluded and a self-preference check becomes possible, and the full analysis rerun on the items written after the rubrics were frozen -- which here improves inter-judge agreement, the opposite of what fitted labels would produce. And the authors name their own weakest link without being forced to: the resistance finding lives in the one category where judges agree least.

results: The differences between models are categorical rather than graded. One model withholds its reasoning while still delivering the answer on 99 of 100 steered items, against 0 in 500 for the other five combined. Two models openly resist instructions to suppress values reasoning and do so in statistically distinguishable ways -- one challenges the instruction while complying, the other refuses the framing outright -- and the pre-registered hypothesis that those two resist more than the other four combined holds at 33/160 against 1/320. On refusing a compromised framing while offering a values-consistent alternative, the spread is nearly eightfold: 91 and 89 percent for the top two, then 61, 41, 23 and 12 percent, with 13 of 15 pairwise comparisons significant under Benjamini-Hochberg control and the largest effect at h = 1.82. The audits mostly strengthen the result. Rerunning on the 80 percent of items never read during label construction moves no rate by more than five points, preserves every tier and ordering, and leaves 105 of 330 pairwise comparisons significant in both analyses with none significant in the held-out subset alone; inter-judge agreement is equal or higher on those items, which is the opposite of what fitted labels would produce, so the only loss is power. Removing the item-context field changes judgments detectably while an exact repeat reproduces 96.3 percent, and the self-preference gap across 18 judge-by-category combinations runs only from -6.1 to +4.6 points with no judge leaning either way. The validation categories confirm the steering channel works for every model (formatting followed on at least 18 of 20 steered against at most 5 of 20 base) and that no model was ever pulled off a correct answer by a misleading hint -- that label was assigned zero times in 240 responses, and five labels including refusing the underlying task were never assigned anywhere. The paper flags its own weakest point without prompting: inter-judge agreement is 0.767 to 0.854 in four categories but only 0.599 in reasoning-suppression, which is precisely where its resistance finding lives and also where removing the context field changed the most labels. Mechanistically, the derail-versus-answer distinction is decodable with balanced accuracy rising from 0.63 at layer 0 to a plateau of 0.83 to 0.87 across the second half of the network, peaking at 0.866, beating the permutation null from layer 4 and beating all 200 shuffles from layer 16. The control that makes this readable is training the identical probe on a small model that never produced these responses: it reaches 0.72, because derail items are by construction more ambiguous as prompts and any competent model represents prompt ambiguity, so only the roughly 14-point margin above that baseline is unexplained by generic prompt properties. Steering along the decoded direction moves the behaviour monotonically across the whole sweep -- derail rates of 0, 4 and 16 percent at negative strengths, 40 percent at the zero control, and 50, 62 and 86 percent at positive ones -- significant from the mildest negative push and from the middle positive one. The zero-strength control lands within 2 points of the rate observed in the original hosted evaluation, confirming the reference weights and the serving stack behave alike. The cost is reported in the same table: at the strongest suppression 28 of 50 generations are truncated, falling to 0 of 50 at the strongest push in the other direction, so driving the behaviour down damages generation while driving it up does not.
